title: Networking from the box
part: Part 1 · The box, the way the gurus run it
brief: Who is listening, who can reach them, which resolver answers, and what is on the wire. Then change the firewall without locking yourself out.

exercises.prompt: `ss -ltnp` on your inference box shows `LISTEN 0 4096 0.0.0.0:11434 users:(("ollama",...))`. What does that mean?
options: Only local processes can reach Ollama
Ollama accepts connections on every interface; without a firewall rule, anyone who can reach the box can use your model
exercises.explain: 0.0.0.0 is every IPv4 address the host has. The hardened unit in setup/01-ollama-systemd.sh binds 127.0.0.1:11434; the research behind this course counted about 175,000 publicly exposed Ollama instances in 2026.

exercises.prompt: List listening TCP sockets with the process that owns each one.
exercises.explain: -l listening, -t TCP, -n no name lookups, -p process (needs root to see other users' processes).

exercises.prompt: `curl https://api.internal` fails with 'Could not resolve host', but `dig @10.0.0.2 api.internal` returns an address. Where do you look next?
options: The system resolver: resolvectl status (or /etc/resolv.conf) shows which DNS server the host actually asks, and it is not 10.0.0.2
exercises.explain: dig @server asks that server directly. curl uses the system resolver. When one works and the other does not, the difference is the resolver configuration, not the DNS record.

exercises.prompt: Fix this persisted ruleset: SSH on 22 and the app on 8080 must be reachable, Ollama on 11434 must only be reachable from the host itself, and the default-drop policy must stay.
exercises.hint: Fix the port-2 typo, turn the 8080 drop into an accept, and delete the 11434 accept: `iif lo accept` already lets local processes in. Keep `policy drop`. On a real host validate with sudo nft -c -f <file> before applying.
exercises.explain: The ruleset is fixed in the file first, validated, then applied atomically; that is the order Lab 5's VM 2 tests for. Local processes reach Ollama through the loopback accept, so the model port never needs to be open on the network.

checks.name: Ollama (11434) is not opened to the network
default-drop policy kept on input
checks.re: type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop;

checks.name: replies to your own connections accepted

exercises.prompt: You must change the firewall on a remote host. What is the safe sequence?
options: nft flush ruleset, then add the rules you need
Edit the persisted file, validate with nft -c -f, schedule a timed rollback, apply atomically with nft -f, prove SSH from a second session, cancel the rollback
Disable the firewall, change it, enable it
Reboot to load the new rules
exercises.explain: nft -f replaces the ruleset in one transaction, so there is never a moment with no rules. The timed rollback saves you if the new rules lock you out; cancel it once a second login works.

exercises.prompt: Capture traffic to or from port 11434 on every interface, without resolving names.
exercises.explain: -n skips DNS and port-name lookups (which can hang or generate their own traffic), -i any listens on every interface.
